title: They didn’t crucify Jesus for silence.
paragraphs:
They didn’t crucify Jesus for silence.
They crucified Him for speaking without permission.

No license.
No rabbinical stamp.
No religious approval.
Just truth.
And it made the system uncomfortable.
“They were astonished… saying, ‘How does this Man know letters, having never studied?’” — John 7:15
Sound familiar?

Today, you share the Word…
and they ask for your credentials.

“Where did you study?”
“Who ordained you?”
“Under what authority?”
But here’s the tension—
Truth doesn’t wait for a certificate.

Fishermen preached.
Tax collectors testified.
A Samaritan woman evangelized a whole city—right after meeting Jesus.

No seminary.
No platform.
Just encounter.
But here’s what we must not miss…

This is not rebellion against the Church.
This is a reminder of what the Church was meant to be.

“Yes, some scholars interpret authority as something that must be recognized and tested within the body of Christ.”
And that matters—because God is not a God of disorder (1 Corinthians 14:33).
But authority in Scripture is not built on titles.
It’s built on truth, calling, and fruit.

Jesus said:
“Whoever does the will of My Father… is My brother and sister and mother.” — Matthew 12:50

Not whoever has the loudest title.
Not whoever owns the building.
Whoever obeys.

So yes—be humble.
Be teachable.
Stay rooted in Scripture.
But don’t let fear silence you when God has clearly spoken through His Word.
Because the same Spirit that raised Christ from the dead…
now lives in you.

And if what you speak is anchored in Scripture,
centered on Christ,
and pointing people to repentance and grace—
then you are not speaking out of rebellion.
You are walking in obedience.
The problem isn’t that truth is being shared.
The problem is who controls the microphone.
And Jesus never asked permission to preach the Kingdom.
He simply obeyed the Father.
So should we.
Someone you know is being silenced right now.
